Remember one principle: machines mix materials and control curing, while skilled hands place fabric and remove bubbles. Much of a part's quality depends on the laminator's craft.
It is a poor fit for people who dislike dust, resin odors, and physically demanding factory work or expect a clean office. Poor protection can cause long-term health harm.

A common path is: enter through vocational school or an apprenticeship, begin as a layup assistant, learn cutting, resin mixing, and fabric placement, master demolding and sanding, then advance into inspection, process, or composite-technician roles.
This occupation suits patient people with strong hands-on ability who can accept workshop conditions. Workers learn quickly if they can place layers without bubbles and maintain even thickness.

Fiberglass Laminators And Fabricators place fiberglass cloth and resin in layers, compact and cure them into composite parts, then demold, trim, and sand the products. Their manual work forms a core stage in composite manufacturing.

entries: Fiberglass Laminators And Fabricators place fiberglass cloth and resin in layers, compact and cure them into composite parts, then demold, trim, and sand the products. Their manual work forms a core stage in composite manufacturing.

paragraphs: Workers begin by collecting materials from process sheets, cutting cloth, and mixing resin. They kneel by molds to place layer after layer. Large parts take most of a day and require speed, bubble removal, and even thickness. During curing, workers make smaller parts. After demolding, they trim and sand amid dust and noise, wearing respirators and eye protection throughout.

In one sentence, they form composite parts on molds using fiberglass cloth and resin. They cut cloth, mix resin, place layers, remove bubbles, cure and demold, trim and sand, inspect quality, and record processes.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 18,600 Fiberglass Laminators And Fabricators were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 19,400 by 2034, a net increase of about 800 jobs, with about 2,100 openings each year. The median annual wage was about $45,800 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not eliminate Fiberglass Laminators And Fabricators, but it will change the process. Systems absorb layup planning, material calculations, and cure monitoring. Automated fiber and tape placement (AFP/ATL) also handles some standardized large parts. Small batches, complex shapes, and finishing on large parts still depend on manual work because machines cannot soon replicate the required feel.

paragraphs: A score of 4/10 indicates low-moderate AI exposure. Systems increasingly handle the occupation's limited desk work, including scheduling, material calculations, and inspection records.

Low-moderate exposure does not mean high risk. Automated placement targets standardized large parts, while small batches, complex shapes, and manual finishing remain necessary. Repetitive simple layup faces pressure, while skilled workers who read drawings and understand processes gain value.

If you prefer a vocational route, study composites or molds and seek internships at wind-blade plants or shipyards. Practice layup and drawing interpretation, then learn process fundamentals to advance toward technician roles.

Learn process parameters, inspection standards, and new equipment such as automated placement and vision inspection. Advancing from layup execution to process and inspection skills reduces exposure to repetitive-task automation.
Workers without experience can start as layup assistants and learn cutting and resin mixing. Resumes should quantify products completed, yield achieved, and processes mastered.

Do not hire laminators only for willingness to work. Assess yield and process understanding. Workers who read drawings, control bubbles and delamination, and collaborate with new equipment are worth retaining.

subject.summary: Fiberglass laminators are craftspeople who make composite materials by hand. Boat hulls, wind blades, and vehicle parts are built layer by layer through their work.
